thread:
alex: Quick check — where can I pull the per-pool autoscale + saturation graph for the new eu-west-2 dedicated pool? saw a short blip of 503s around 10:12 UTC and want to correlate with scaling events.

maria: Grafana has the per-pool view. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pools-eu?panelId=7 — looks at 'pool_inflight' and 'pool_scale_events'. Start with panel 7 for autoscale timeline.

sam: Also check the 'queue_depth' and 'serve_latency_p50/p95' panels on the same board. 503s usually line up with queue spikes.

alex: thanks — where are the raw logs for the worker instances tied to that pool? want traces for 10:10–10:20.

jin: Logs live in Loki under label {pool="eu-west-2-dedicated"}. Quick query: `{job="redwood-runtime", pool="eu-west-2-dedicated"} |= "503" | ts` — that'll surface requests that returned 503.

maria: For traces, use Jaeger link: https://traces.internal/redwood/search?service=runtime&tags.pool=eu-west-2-dedicated&start=2155000000&end=2155000800 — filter for span name `inference.request` and look for long tail.

alex: perfect. any idea which saturation signal we should tune — cpu, kv-cache hit-rate, or inflight?

sam: In our recent incidents, inflight per-GPU and kv_cache_evictions were the leading indicators. If inflight > 1200 per pool for >2m it's usually saturation. kv_cache_evictions spikes precede higher p95 by ~30s.

taylor: Can we get a short-lived monitor that alerts when (pool_inflight > 1100 AND kv_cache_evictions_rate > 0.1) for 90s? That would've caught this one earlier.

jin: Proposed Datadog monitor (draft):
```
avg(last_2m):
  (max:pool.inflight{pool:eu-west-2-dedicated} by {pool} > 1100)
AND
  (increase(pool.kv_cache_evictions_total{pool:eu-west-2-dedicated}[1m]) / sum:increase(pool.kv_cache_accesses_total{pool:eu-west-2-dedicated}[1m]) > 0.1)
```
Set notify: eng-platform-oncall + #eng-platform.

maria: Minor note — some bursty jobs (batch scoring) can briefly push inflight; we should silence if origin:batch-worker label present. Add `!origin:batch-worker` to the monitor scope.

alex: good call. also, how do we distinguish autoscale probe-caused spikes vs real load?

sam: Look at `scale_probe_count` on the timeline. Probe bursts have near-zero payload latency and short-lived request shapes. Real load shows sustained p95 increase and token throughput drop.

obs-bot: New dashboard snapshot created for eu-west-2: https://grafana.internal/snapshot/abc123 (expires in 7d) :white_check_mark:

alex: ok next actions: jin to post the Loki query + Jaeger link in the incident ticket; sam to add the probe vs load filter to the dashboard; taylor to greenlight the proposed monitor (with batch-worker silence). I'll triage traces and update ticket by EOD. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll also add a short note to the per-pool runbook about kv_cache_evictions as an early signal.

alex: thanks team — ping me if you want me to escalate to infra for more headroom.
